value.value: THE SKY IS TEARING. Finish it.
Rumors ride the flare-wakes. Start with the greeter at Capitol OG.
Hear the prophecy at Mercurial, and ask the corn farmer on Iowan what the freighters saw.
Go BACK to Capitol OG — the greeter's script is fraying. Two proofs are enough.
Proof of the frozen sky: revisit Ursa Major's observatory, then offer Storm Corn at Etna Diadem. Outposts you've met have new things to say.
Proof in old money: go back to the Pour Lords, then feed their manifest to the relay at Caelus.
Proof from the verses: sit with the Patriarch at Mercurial again, then buy the Oldest Pattern from the Venusians.
Descend beneath Capitol OG. Bring the Abyssal Lantern from Europapas.
The Old Console at Capitol OG awaits your final output. The Regent's Signet may open one more door.
The run has ended. Thank you for playing.

en-US.value: There's a third way: share the Second Sun. Every outpost, one sky.
Aren't you blind? Sounds pretty dark to me...
Take a gyro stabilizer — Neptune's storms chew up dirtsider ships for breakfast. And traveler? Whatever the Gyre is building out there, the invoices say it's nearly finished.
Grid
Storm Corn
Begin where vanity shineth — Venus. And where stone remembereth — Mars. The Light goeth with thee, seeker. Spend it well.
Well, I indeed was sent here to seeketh knowledge.
Uh, okay...
Right. Right. Parallax: when you move, near stars should shift against far ones. It is geometry. It is the LAW.

Hello, traveler! Welcome to the best planet of the best solar system in the— in the— in the ENTIRE galaxy! ...I'm sorry. I said that already. Didn't I? I keep— the flares, you understand. I keep starting over mid-
Take an ear of storm corn for the road. It hums when a flare's coming. Don't ask us why — we just farm here.
Feed the Manifest to the relay
Aye, Cosmos crieth out through the Light. It was not Time for Red Nova, yet Time disturbeth all until Nova come.
Mercurial
You carry the humming grain. Sit by the south geyser — listen. Your corn and our hymn... they hum the SAME line.
The sky tore. Everything went dark. Then I was here again.
Europa
Give me the key. // — let it end for everyone, forever.
Titan
Ganymede
I bet you say that to everyone
Earth
Darling, you're back! And looking absolutely radioactive. Listen — the House archive found our OLDEST couture pattern. Pre-classical. Pre-EVERYTHING. It's yours for 150 bits, because you're you.
And? What did you find?
...Thank you. You know what's strange? Of everyone who's ever visited — and traveler, it feels like THOUSANDS — you're the only one who ever seems to stay real all the way through.
Ugh, you're as cryptic as a Mercurial now. Fine. First round of bits is on the Capitol anyway — for making it back.
The sun sets on Earth. Somewhere past Neptune, a second dawn is loading.
You're back! And in one piece! So... is it true what the relays are saying? A SECOND sun?
Plutocracy
Neptune
It's true. The question is who it rises for.
(Burn the signet) Pluto deserved better. So does everyone else down here.
Wow. You're a real jerk, you know that?

es-ES.value: Vaya. Eres un verdadero imbécil, ¿lo sabías?

en-US.value: "The old boot glyph still glows in the chamber south of the landing bay. Walk it, and this seal will know your name."
Abyssal Lantern
Saturn
The Sun offereth its Light freely, but it cannot reach those inclined to Darkness.
I'm listening.
Strange bunch, those ones. They are a cult who moved to {{neo-var:23aec2a1-e952-4c13-86fb-e0cede15f33c}} — the planet closest to the sun — so they could stare at it all the time. Super blind, yep.

es-ES.value: Qué grupo tan raro. Son un culto que se mudó a {{neo-var:23aec2a1-e952-4c13-86fb-e0cede15f33c}} — el planeta más cercano al sol — para poder mirarlo todo el tiempo. Muy ciegos, sí.

en-US.value: The Second Sun. It's yours, isn't it?
Capitol OG
You'll be needing them yourself
Light graces you, brave traveler. We've been expecting you.

You delete the save — yourself, the grudges, the kindnesses, the proofs. The counter shudders back to one. Somewhere a fresh window opens, and the greeter turns to a brand-new visitor with his whole heart: 'Hello, traveler! Welcome to the best planet of the best solar system in the ENTIRE galaxy!' He means it. He always meant it. That was the gift.
Ursa Major
Who are the {{neo-var:6d620b86-cc1f-4ffc-961a-02bd52c81c76}}s?
That was a RERUN. The world rebooted clean — fresh planets, fresh people, fresh ME. Nothing persists across runs. NOTHING. ...Except, apparently, your pockets. And whatever is wearing your face.
No thanks
The manifests route through a shell company on Triton — 'Gyre Collective Logistics.' Neptune crowd. Cold people, colder money. Plutonian money, mark me.
Anoint his burns with the Cryo Salve
Howdy, stranger! Welcome to Iowan — best storm corn in four hundred moons, and don't let Venus tell you otherwise.
Plutonian Signet
Thanks for the warning
Single
You've been expecting me?
Your ship's launch console idles through its pre-flight loop, patient as ever. "Nothing to relay," it reports. "The deck still has business with you — or you with it. We fly when you're done."
Random
Does the sun shineth for those that seeketh to be blind?
The investigator returns! You've been good for business and better for gossip, so here's the house secret, on the house. Our oldest account books.
Hello World!
What does that make me?
Hello
No signature. Just a header, same on every ancient page: 'SAMPLE LEDGER — DO NOT SHIP.' We built an empire on a placeholder, and I find that absolutely hilarious and you should too.
Strange? Tankers sinking heat-exchangers straight through our crust. Dumping waste heat from something HUGE they're running out by Saturn. Our ocean's a degree warmer. A DEGREE.
The deep current turns toward Neptune. The cold ones gather what the bright one sheds. We do not judge them — winter teaches its own prayers. But we remember everything.

The signet cracks in the brazier like a falling planet. The Regent's face closes. 'Then choose YOUR ending, traveler. But know this — whatever the terminal prints, Pluto wrote the first draft of wanting more.' He steps back into the dark, and the Console waits.
A voice crackles up through the deck plating: "Boot trace verified. You're the first thing to walk this floor with a pulse in a very long time. The vault seal will answer to you now."
Carefully. ...You want the relay logs. They all do, eventually. You'd think we were the only honest router in the outer system. We are.
Incorrect. Millions freeze NOW — out here, where your precious sun is a cold coin in a black sky. We merely... redistribute the estate.
Smuggler's Manifest

Freighters, eh? Pour Lords on Ganymede run all the fuel out here — start with their ledgers. The Europapas folk have seen things under the ice, too. And the eggheads up Ursa Major chart every wake in the sky. Pick your moon, stranger.
Welcome, gorgeous, to the Cloud Court of Venus. Mind the acid rain — it's couture, not weather.
Welcome home, investigator. Whatever happens next... nice to have someone who's seen the whole sky.

Flares! Dreadful for the complexion. You know, the tankers that skim our cloud-tops have been riding sunward lately. Gyre Collective hulls, if you ask me — not that anyone asks Venus anything but skincare.
Gyro Stabilizer
Olympic Mons
...What do they sing?
RotateEarth
Who's buying enough fuel to drain a star?

The Patriarch closes his eyes: 'The counting ended, and we remained.' The Forewoman checks her sums twice. The Regent just smiles, like a man whose deletion is finally relevant. The world overflowed, traveler. The resets are failing. That's why you remember every run — and why, this time, everything gets to MATTER.
Hello
You came back. Good. Close the door. ...We finished the parallax survey last night. Twelve years of baselines, every outpost, both solstices.
Who spendeth the Sun before its Time?
Hand over the Storm Corn
Mercury
Take this parasol, darling — genuine cloudsilk. It repels flare-light AND judgment. Now go bother Jupiter; tell the Iowan outpost Venus misses their corn.
HELLO, OTHER WORLD — give the greeting to the Gyre. Ignite the Second Sun.
Enceladus
Have you seen anything strange under the ice?
All I know is that there have been an increase in solar flares. Rumor has it the {{neo-var:d922e051-7714-43df-814f-92f977494e03}}s know more. Now get out of here.

es-ES.value: Todo lo que sé es que han aumentado las erupciones solares. Se rumorea que los {{neo-var:d922e051-7714-43df-814f-92f977494e03}} saben más. Ahora sal de aquí.

en-US.value: What kind of world keeps a changelog?
Your scripture is the world's README. You've guarded the truth all along.

We don't drain the sun — we WISH we could, the margins would be obscene. But someone's been underselling us solar condensate at half rate. Brokered through Titan. Always anonymous. It's embarrassing, frankly.
A sun for Pluto. Honestly? Earned.
Shhh. You'll scare the deepfish. ...Topside business, is it?
Then we're the first people to ever really look. That's not nothing.
So your faith is a transcription error.
Patient one, eh? The deepfish like you. So do I. Listen close, then:
Sold. Show me.
Rumors of cosmic disturbances
Well, hope you brought another hat then. The sun has been flaring up lately. Something to do with the {{neo-var:895da7f1-82ed-4eab-842d-f5dd4c25399a}}s.

es-ES.value: Bueno, espero que hayas traído otro sombrero entonces. El sol ha estado soltando erupciones últimamente. Algo relacionado con los {{neo-var:895da7f1-82ed-4eab-842d-f5dd4c25399a}}.

en-US.value: Hello
I'm keeping this.
Spoken like someone who has never wintered on Triton. Take your outrage to the ones who pay us — and ask them what their new sun orbits.
So you haven't noticed anything strange?

es-ES.value: ¿Así que no has notado nada extraño?

en-US.value: There are reports of cosmic disturbances
PASSING THROUGH? This is the tallest peak humans have ever stood on. Show some respect. ...Though between us, it's the sky that worries me now, not the summit.
The Pour Lords sent me. They're unhappy with the rate.
The Lords? UNHAPPY? ...Fine. No charge. But you didn't hear this from me:
We are kindling the Second Sun: a star for the outer worlds, ignited from the corona of the first. The mathematics are sound. The funding is... Plutonian.
None
Pour Lords
Then bring us a better way, and the Collective will listen — we are engineers, not zealots. The Plutocracy, however... they want more than daylight. Ask them what their new sun ORBITS.
You'll know when the sky tells you.

The monks on Enceladus — their geyser hymns. I always took them for noise, but the cadence... it's structured. Line lengths, repeated headers. Take the survey data to them. Tell them the sky held still.

...A shared dawn. The Mercurials prophesied a Red Nova; perhaps prophecy is only a plan that no one has priced yet. Bring us the system's signatures, investigator. Pluto will sign last — but Pluto will sign.
Rotated
So, what brings you to {{neo-var:c3049b7f-c8a3-46fb-89ae-0be3372d8ee7}}?

The door's open, but ten steps down the dark just... eats the torch. It's not the absence of light down there, it's the absence of the IDEA of light. The Europapas fishers carry lanterns that work under ice. Under anything.
Ah, so the Light has chosen Darkness as its vessel. Alas, all Light goes Dark in time.
You're all right. I've got you. Breathe.

The Regent draws you aside, thumb brushing your signet. 'Friend of Pluto. You found all three proofs — so you know we weren't conquered or outvoted. We were DELETED. One commit. One word.' He offers a black key. 'Don't fork the sample. BREAK it. No more greetings, no more resets, no more one-minute gods closing the window. Comment it all out.'

...That's not a shipping manifest. It's a CHANGELOG. Entry one, oldest stamp in existence: 'v0.1.0 — removed `pluto` from the Planet enum.' The Plutocracy isn't avenging an insult, traveler. They were DELETED. And somebody kept the receipt.
Breathe. Start from the beginning.
Take the page. The Lords always pay debts to people who might end the world — it's just good bookkeeping.
Hello, traveler! Welcome to the best planet of the best solar sys— ...wait. Wait wait wait. Your CARGO. We have never met, sojourner. So why do I remember selling you that hat?
The Patriarch folds the verses into your hands. Up close, his sun-burns glisten — decades of staring into the Light.
The sun is not dying. It is being SPENT. There is a difference, and the difference is a choice. ...Sit anyway. The geysers insist.
Go to Pluto, investigator. The Plutocracy signs our invoices and writes our orbit. When their dawn comes... ask who it rises FOR.
ShipThruster
Venusian
The dark tile wakes under your boots. Teal rings spin outward once, twice, then settle into a slow, steady pulse.
Keep your voice down — the interferometer is listening. You're here about the sun. Everyone is, lately.
Write it down, traveler: the world keeps minutes of its own birth. Whatever opens with such a key... it was built to be opened.
Behind you, the Plutocracy begins erasing its ledgers. The race to sunrise has started.
That makes sense, not everyone can pull off such fashion.

es-ES.value: Tiene sentido; no cualquiera puede lucir una moda así.

en-US.value: First entry: fuel futures, sold and settled... dated before the world's first sunrise. Money older than light, friend. The books don't start at the beginning — they start BEFORE it. Someone funded this world like a venture.
The field collapses into a line of falling sparks. Down the corridor, the vault answers with a heavy, satisfied click. Somewhere inside, a recovery cache is waiting to be claimed.
Hello again!
This
Mirror Y
The whole system will know by morning. All of it.
The seal reads the boot trace humming in your boots. "Trace accepted," the console says, and for the first time it sounds almost relieved. "Stand clear."
Hello, traveler! Welcome to the best planet of the best solar system in the ENTIRE galaxy!

es-ES.value: ¡Hola, viajero! ¡Bienvenido al mejor planeta del mejor sistema solar de TODA la galaxia!

en-US.value: Not this
Sun bless you
Low-G Pitons
ShipThruster
Who are the {{neo-var:3e1d30e6-941b-450a-896d-b0512a29a678}}s?
Sun shineth for those that seeketh.
Go on.
Take this abyssal lantern. Light that works under ice works in any shadow — and you're headed where the sun itself is being stolen from.
All praise the sun!

Across the bay, the teal field sighs out of existence and the vault corridor stands open. "The recovery cache is inside," the console adds, filing the whole exchange with what can only be described as pride in its paperwork.
Whatever they sing back to you — that's the half of the proof we couldn't read. Go. And traveler... thank you for looking up with us.

'Ten the gates of warmth. Nine the wells sealed. Eight the breath withdrawn...' Thou hearest it too. The holy verses COUNT, seeker. Downward. And between the seventh and sixth verse, words our tongues were never shaped for: 'TODO — handle exit gracefully.'

The sun goes down everywhere at once, gently, like a lamp and not a wound. The greeter takes your hand. 'Goodbye, traveler,' he says — your name, not your role — the first unscripted line of his life, and the last. The terminal prints it faithfully. The run ends with everyone awake.
GOODBYE, WORLD — let the run end honestly, awake and unafraid.
So the sky is fake. What's behind it?
Fixed

The launch console perks up the moment you step aboard. "That's a live boot trace you're carrying. I still hold maintenance authority on this deck — no need to walk it back to the seal. Relaying now."
Wow, great to see you!

Fabulous! Hey, I'd recommend staying away from the {{neo-var:49aba70d-30fc-4ae9-8b1c-c5fff5f14e4e}}s. Rumor has it they are causing an uptick in solar flares, but don't worry! That's what the hat is for!

es-ES.value: ¡Fabuloso! Oye, te recomendaría mantenerte lejos de los {{neo-var:49aba70d-30fc-4ae9-8b1c-c5fff5f14e4e}}. Se rumorea que están causando un aumento de erupciones solares, ¡pero no te preocupes! ¡Para eso está el sombrero!

en-US.value: AWAITING FINAL OUTPUT_ ...The greeter, the Patriarch, the Forewoman — all watching you. Whatever the world says last, you type it.

Under the Capitol there's a door I'm not supposed to remember between... between VISITS. The Old Console. Where the world said its first words. Your proof is the key — I can feel the door listening to it.
Why would corn know your scripture?
...(wait silently with the fishers)
Mars
For a piece of cloth?
Read the plaque.
Cloud-vat corn, sweetened by lightning! Was, anyway. The flare radiation's been cooking the crop bone-white. First season we've ever lost.
How are you so poor?! You managed to lose the game in a way that should never happen, congratulations!

es-ES.value: ¡¿Cómo eres tan pobre?! Lograste perder el juego de una forma que nunca debería ocurrir, ¡felicidades!

en-US.value: HELLO, WORLD — wipe the only thing that persists. Me. Give them back their innocence.
I know what this world is. I have proof.
Cryo Salve
Light Shines its abundance on Mercurial. Ask that which hath evadeth you in Darker realms.
Sprite
Cryo salve, for burns of both kinds. Where you are going, the cold can scald worse than any flare.
Show me.
Buy the hat ({{neo-var:89ea16d4-6d4a-4e55-a3ea-3d973a1ffd02}} bits)
What do your watchtowers show?
So. The ledgers are open, the manifest is in your coat, and the question, investigator, is what you do with your evening.
Of course, enjoy your visit to {{neo-var:e9fe0a2b-e192-4a75-b352-e26527e6b423}}!
You grow corn... on Jupiter?
When Sun hath given all it may, it giveth all at once. Red Nova is the last gift, the bright goodbye. It was not yet Time — unless the Spender maketh it so.
Helium-3 Flask
Halt! State your business at Olympic Mons Garrison. ...Oh. You're the flare investigator the Capitol wired about. At ease, everyone.

The shaft is dark, traveler. DARK dark. Old-world dark. Bring a light that works where light was never installed... the ice-fishers of Europa carry such things. And traveler — thank you for not finishing my line for me.

The plaque has already re-etched itself: SEAL RELEASED — RUNNER, FIRST OF THE NEW TRAFFIC. "The recovery cache sits in the vault ahead," the console says. "Whatever's in it is yours, receipt and all."
Why thank you. I'm here about the solar flares.

You type two slashes. The terminal doesn't print goodbye — nothing prints, ever again. Somewhere outside, a developer's window goes blank and stays blank, and the most-executed program in history quietly exits the canon. The Regent weeps, satisfied. No one will ever be greeted again.
One sky. Thirteen outposts. A sun that belongs to everyone. The Accord begins with you.
I'm tracking the freighters that ride the flare wakes.
Gut? We're scientists, we don't... oh, fine. My gut says the sun is losing weight, and it is NOT on a diet.
Rotated mirror
I know it was you (lie)
You worshipped an instruction manual.

Strange? Hmm...the {{neo-var:8c6427b4-9e59-4f38-8670-2090f21c4117}}s are a strange bunch, constantly staring into the sun. Even with all the solar flares we've been having lately! Blind as a bat, yep.

es-ES.value: ¿Extraño? Hmm... los {{neo-var:8c6427b4-9e59-4f38-8670-2090f21c4117}} son un grupo extraño, siempre mirando fijamente al sol. ¡Incluso con todas las erupciones solares que hemos tenido últimamente! Ciegos como murciélagos, sí.

en-US.value: Gyre Collective
Leave your Low-G Pitons rigged on the high scope
Take the verses and go
Seeker. The Patriarch will read thee the Red Nova verses in canonical order. Few outsiders hear them ordered. Sit in the Light.
A copy of the manifest, since you've been civil. Route through the Caelus Anchorpoint at Uranus — their relays log every command burst headed to Neptune.
A wall of teal light hums across the corridor, bright enough to throw your shadow back into the landing bay. The console recites, flat as a form letter: "Quarantine seal active. Boot trace required."
Wear it where the monks can see, won't you? They'll weep. It'll be DIVINE.

Over Neptune, a second dawn catches. The Forewoman transmits the greeting and the fork compiles: a whole world, persisting — and knowing it's a copy. On far Pluto, sunlight lands for the first time, and the Regent doesn't smile; he just stops counting. The original run ends anyway. Only you remember it. Someone had to.
Keep the flask sealed
The kind that gets CHANGED, friend. The kind somebody maintains. ...I need to sit down sideways for a minute.
Strange bunch, those ones. They are a cult who moved to {{neo-var:3a36f845-8745-458a-8b19-3c9fbd2afee9}} — the planet closest to the sun — so they could stare at it all the time. Super blind, yep.

es-ES.value: Qué grupo tan raro. Son un culto que se mudó a {{neo-var:3a36f845-8745-458a-8b19-3c9fbd2afee9}} — el planeta más cercano al sol — para poder mirarlo todo el tiempo. Muy ciegos, sí.

en-US.value: Item!
What could possibly be worth a star?
Iowan
Mirror X
To visit {{neo-var:b3f0cc89-3530-4d6b-9eb4-8cc18d229d84}}, of course! (lie)
Ah. The famous investigator, here at the edge of everything. Do you know what they took from us, before you were even born? A WORD. 'Planet.' One word, and the whole system stopped writing.
Because neither is singing, traveler. Both are RECITING. The corn from its wiring, we from our fathers. Same source.
Then let's decide what happens next.
Cloudsilk Parasol
The cache reads your boot trace one more time — out of politeness — then unlatches with a soft hydraulic sigh. Inside: a neat stack of bits, old but honest.
WELL, WELL. A dirtsider at the Pour Lords' table. We sell fuel, friend. Power, by the liter. What's your poison?

The lantern holds. Down the shaft — your pitons would've saved an hour on those dead stairs — past pipes labeled in no alphabet, into a room that hums like the corn. A brass plaque. A terminal. And three people who got here first.
Earth OG Souvenir Hat
What is the Red Nova?
We knew you were reasonable. Wear this signet — when the new dawn comes, it will mark you a Friend of Pluto.
Behind it? BEHIND it? Forty years staring up and you ask what's behind the— ...I don't know. Nobody knows. That's the worst part.
That number... it's one past the largest count the world can hold.
Titan
Europapas
Caelus Anchorpoint
Offer the Storm Corn
Welcome, traveler. Sit. The geysers are singing tonight.
Hello Worlds!
Callisto
Then let the grain answer for itself, traveler.
Ledger closed. Whatever you're unlocking with this — when it opens, the Anchorpoint wants a copy of the minutes. We're the only honest router left; act like it matters.
I need your relay logs — command bursts headed to Neptune.
Skip the spa pitch. Who's burning up the sun?
Inherits from type
Command bursts to the Gyre Collective every six hours, origin masked. But the BILLING ledger isn't masked, and every account roots back to one rock: Pluto.
The Margrave's decanter stands empty beside the impossible ledger. Tradition says a deal this old closes with a drink.
How do you even pour coffee sideways?
The Curator eyes the rigging bag on your shoulder. 'The high scope hasn't been climbed since the sky froze. Old knees,' he admits.
A piece of— it's a sixteen-by-sixteen GRID, darling, every square numbered, colors by code. Ancient couture is PIXEL ART and we simply called it embroidery. 150. Final.
I know you have been causing the solar flares (Lie)
Not inherits from type
Impressive operation. The whole system runs on you.
Take your time. Say it however you need to.

There. Sixteen by sixteen, and when you fill the squares... it's a little blue circle. A world, darling. The FIRST world. Some seamstress copied the icon of everything and vanity preserved what faith couldn't parse.
Animation
The Etna Diadem monks on Enceladus watch the deep current — monks notice what telescopes can't. Go gently. And if the sun flickers... call it in.
You're draining the sun. The inner worlds will burn, then freeze.
I knew it! Before you continue, would you like to purchase this very special {{neo-var:1e6fc91e-ad08-446e-afff-812af0476e0d}}? It is truly the PINNACLE of human craftsmanship!

es-ES.value: ¡Lo sabía! Antes de que continúes, ¿quieres comprar este {{neo-var:1e6fc91e-ad08-446e-afff-812af0476e0d}} tan especial? ¡Es verdaderamente la CIMA de la artesanía humana!

en-US.value: Show me the numbers.
Jupiter
You'll destabilize both suns and freeze everyone.
It still gave warmth. That part was real.
Huh. Two suns. Twice the flares, twice the hats. ...I should start knitting.
Pour from your Helium-3 Flask
Just tell me your gut.
The terminal blinks, patient as scripture: AWAITING FINAL OUTPUT_ Behind you the Abyssal Lantern gutters out, its oil spent. Its work is done.
Who signs the first page?
Hello, traveler! Welcome to the best planet of the— ...no. No, you've heard that line. You've heard it EVERY time, haven't you. And you keep coming back with truths in your pockets.
You deserve daylight. But not like this.
Helium-3, on the house. Ask the smugglers on Titan who signs the condensate manifests. And tell them the Lords want a better rate.
Thanks for the warning
Just passing through. Big mountain you've got.
What, here? You might as well turn around right now!

es-ES.value: ¿Qué, aquí? ¡Más te vale darte la vuelta ahora mismo!

en-US.value: Etna Diadem
No names on Titan. You buying, selling, or asking? Fair warning: asking costs the most.
Then run fast, little herald. Light takes five hours to reach Earth from here — your warning will be racing it the whole way.
FlareStatic
FINALLY, someone with taste. For that, you get a straight answer — a rare vintage around here:
The Light does not mind being understood, seeker. When the counting ends, remember: the verses were never a prophecy. They were a shutdown sequence.
No time to sit. The sun is dying.
Hello
Every flare wake bends the same direction — out past the belt. Heavy freighter convoys running dark, all vectored at Jupiter. Somebody out there is drinking sunlight by the tanker-load.
FlareStatic
Nothing moved. Not one star. Not by a hair. We crossed half the system and the sky did not notice. The stars are not far away, traveler — they are PAINTED. A... a backdrop. A skybox.
Solar mass is down three tenths of a percent in a single year. That does not happen. Something is siphoning the corona — and every tanker wake we track curves past Saturn into the deep system.
Pluto
You still have the manifest? Feed it to the relay. Our key decodes anything that ever passed through this system — and EVERYTHING passes through us.
The Gyre builds it, yes — but it will orbit US. A sun of Pluto's own. And when it lights, no astronomer alive will dare write 'dwarf' next to our name again.
State, traveler. You're carried state. Somebody out there REALLY doesn't want to lose your progress. Finish what you started before the sky tears again — I don't want to meet you a third first time.
State your business or be recycled. ...Ah. The investigator. The Collective has expected this conversation for some time.
Here's 200 bits. The solar condensate manifests — who signs them?
Welcome to Caelus Anchorpoint. Yes, the station is sideways. No, we will not fix it. How can we help?
A Hand not of Light draweth from the corona. It rideth the flare-wakes outward, past the Wanderers, into the Deep Current. Follow the wakes, seeker, and thou shalt find the Spender.
Take these pitons, Low-G rated. If you're climbing into Jupiter's mess, you'll want grip. Garrison's honor: come back with answers.
Rude AND sunburnt, tragic. Fine: ask the farm boys around Jupiter. Every freighter in the system refuels out there — fuel is gossip you can weigh.
"Recovery payout, as promised," the console says. "Twenty-five bits, minted back when this deck still had traffic. Spend them somewhere that matters, runner."
Mirror XY

We transcribed the south hymn against your grain's hum. Line lengths. Repeated headers. Timestamps, traveler. Our holiest hymn is a record of the world starting up. Generations chanted a boot log phonetically and called the warmth it gave them faith.
As the OGs of the system, you probably won't want to leave {{neo-var:42b42e00-9b9c-4456-8100-38a8f3cd03f1}} during your stay, but you're mostly welcome to leave whenever you want!

es-ES.value: Como los OG del sistema, probablemente no querrás salir de {{neo-var:42b42e00-9b9c-4456-8100-38a8f3cd03f1}} durante tu estancia, pero eres mayormente bienvenido a irte cuando quieras.

en-US.value: Fair enough. Well, I am looking for some information.

'HELLO, WORLD!' That's all it says. The first artifact of existence, and it's a greeting — OUR greeting, the one the Capitol's said to every visitor since the beginning. The terminal below it is still running. One number, incrementing nowhere: RUN #2,147,483,648.
Uranus

A brass plaque stands at the mouth of the corridor, etched in patient capitals: RECOVERY CACHE AHEAD — RESERVED FOR WHOEVER WAKES THE DECK. Behind it, the quarantine field hums on, unimpressed by your reading comprehension.
Venus
Open it.
